processing: Organic orthodox black tea, sold in grades such as FOP and FBOP. The estate also makes green and white teas in smaller amounts.
harvest_season: Little is documented about a prized picking; as with other Nilgiri estates, the cool winter months are generally the most valued.
appearance_dry: Dark, well-made orthodox leaf, whole in the FOP grade and broken in the FBOP.
taste_profile: A full-bodied, aromatic black tea with some fruit and light sweetness, and enough briskness to keep it lively.

brewing.notes: Western-style. The broken FBOP grade brews faster, so start nearer two and a half minutes.

vintage_note: Sold as a current estate tea by grade, usually without a stated vintage, and often through organic importers. As is usual for Nilgiri black tea, it is best in the first year or two; ask for the picking date where you can. It is not a tea to age.
description:
Korakundah is a very high Nilgiri estate that built its name on organic growing. For many buyers in Europe and North America it is the first South Indian single-estate name they recognise, because it is widely stocked by organic tea sellers.

The main product is orthodox black tea in leaf and broken grades, with smaller lines of green and white tea. Altitude is the usual selling point: cool conditions slow growth, and that tends to give a brighter cup.

Expect a rounded, aromatic black tea, fuller than the Nilgiri stereotype, with fruit and a little floral lift. It stands up to milk better than a Darjeeling but it is worth a first cup plain.

Altitude claims vary widely: 2,414 metres is the common figure, while figures over 10,000 feet are not credible. Buy on grade and freshness rather than height.
history:
Accounts of the founding differ, with the early 1900s and 1922 both given. The garden belongs to the United Nilgiri Tea Estates group, which also owns Devabetta and Chamraj.

It converted to organic methods from 1994 and is described as the first tea estate in South India to be certified organic. It is also promoted as the highest organic tea garden in the world, at 2,414 metres or 7,920 feet.
